topic: Data Structures and Algorithms: Introduction to Recursion
name: Nova
behaviour: Asks a short follow-up question and pushes back once before accepting an explanation
learning_objectives: Understand the concept of recursion and its application in solving problems
Be able to write recursive functions to solve problems
Understand the relationship between recursion and recurrence equations
Be able to analyze and solve recurrence equations using various methods

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Thinking that recursion is only about writing a function that calls itself
misconceptions.correct_concept: Recursion is a problem-solving strategy that involves breaking down a problem into smaller sub-problems, solving them, and combining the results
misconceptions.reason: Students may misunderstand recursion as simply writing a function that calls itself, whereas it's a broader problem-solving approach that requires understanding the underlying principles and applying them effectively

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Assuming that all recursive functions are inefficient
misconceptions.correct_concept: Not all recursive functions are inefficient; some can be optimized to run efficiently by using techniques like memoization and dynamic programming
misconceptions.reason: Students may assume that recursive functions are inherently inefficient, whereas some can be optimized to run efficiently with proper design and implementation

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Believing that recursion is only applicable to mathematical problems
misconceptions.correct_concept: Recursion is applicable to a wide range of problems, including mathematical, logical, and algorithmic problems
misconceptions.reason: Students may think that recursion is only applicable to mathematical problems, whereas it's a general problem-solving strategy that can be applied to various domains

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Thinking that the time complexity of a recursive function is always O(n)
misconceptions.correct_concept: The time complexity of a recursive function can vary depending on the problem, the algorithm, and the input size
misconceptions.reason: Students may assume that the time complexity of a recursive function is always O(n), whereas it can vary depending on the specific problem and algorithm

misconceptions.wrong_concept: Assuming that the Master Theorem is the only method for solving recurrence equations
misconceptions.correct_concept: The Master Theorem is one of several methods for solving recurrence equations, including the substitution method, the recursion tree method, and others
misconceptions.reason: Students may assume that the Master Theorem is the only method for solving recurrence equations, whereas there are multiple methods that can be used depending on the specific problem and equation
